newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh and India sign joint venture deals.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh and India sign joint venture deals.

text.p: Bangladeshi and Indian entrepreneurs on Tuesday signed two deals for jointly setting up cement and clinker plants.

Bengal Tiger Cement Ltd of Bangladesh and Narpuh Cement of India's Meghalaya state signed a memorandum of understanding on setting up a joint venture clinker manufacturing unit in Meghalaya, sponsors said.
They said the clinker from the proposed annual 100,000 tonne capacity plant would be bought for Bengal Tiger's cement grinding plant in Bangladesh.
Under the second joint venture deal, Indus Cements Ltd of India's Assam state and Bangladesh's Future Trade Ltd will set up a 100,000 tonne-capacity cement plant in Bangladesh.
The sponsors said they had not yet set any date for beginning work on the plants. They gave no other details.

The agreements were signed in Dhaka following a meeting between the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DCCI) and a visiting delegation of the Federation of Industries of North Eastern Region (FINER) of India.
A 42-member team of the FINER, a forum of businessmen from seven northeastern states of India, is visiting Dhaka to explore trade and economic cooperation with Bangladesh.
India has been asking Dhaka to let it use a trade corridor across Bangladesh that would give it better communication with its hilly and insurgency-ridden northeastern states.
